Stepwise selection of the dependence graph

Source: R/selection.R
mc_graph_stepwise.Rd

Greedy search over supports of the GGM layer guided by an information criterion (see mc_compute_criterion). The backward search starts from the complete graph and, at each step, removes the edge whose removal most reduces the criterion; the forward search starts from the empty graph and adds the edge whose inclusion most reduces it; "both" starts from the complete graph and considers removals and additions at every step. Candidates are ranked by mc_edge_scores (smallest Wald statistic for removal, largest efficient score for addition), and only the k_confirm top-ranked ones are refitted per step, which is the score pruning that keeps the search affordable. The search stops when no candidate lowers the criterion, or after max_steps steps. Because the mean structure is held fixed, only the between-response covariance is refitted at each step, which is justified by the asymptotic orthogonality of the first-stage and graph-layer estimating functions.

Usage

mc_graph_stepwise(
  fit,
  direction = c("backward", "forward", "both"),
  criterion = c("bic", "aic", "qic", "gbic", "clbic", "ebic"),
  max_steps = NULL,
  k_confirm = 3L,
  trace = TRUE,
  ebic_gamma = 0.5,
  cluster = NULL,
  small_sample = FALSE
)

Arguments

fit

an object of class "mcglm_graph" (GGM layer).

direction

"backward" (default), "forward" or "both".

criterion

"bic" (default), "aic", "qic", "gbic" or its alias "clbic", or "ebic".

max_steps

maximum number of steps; NULL (default) means the number of possible edges, \(R(R-1)/2\).

k_confirm

number of top-ranked candidates refitted per step (default 3).

trace

logical; record the accepted moves in the component trace.

ebic_gamma

the parameter of the extended BIC, used only with criterion = "ebic"; see mc_compute_criterion.

cluster

optional independent-cluster identifier, one per residual row, passed to mc_compute_criterion: Pearson contributions are summed within clusters in QIC and GBIC, and the number of clusters replaces the number of rows in the logarithmic penalty of BIC, GBIC and EBIC.

small_sample

logical; apply the cluster factor \(G/(G-1)\), with \(G\) the number of clusters, to the empirical variability of the clustered criteria (default FALSE); ignored without cluster.

Value

An object of class "mcg_selection", a list with method ("stepwise"), criterion, graph (the adjacency matrix of the selected graph), edges (two-column matrix of selected edges), n_edges, trace (data frame with step, action, edge_i, edge_j and criterion for each accepted move, or NULL), fit (the "mcglm_graph" refitted on the selected support) and candidate_failures (data frame of the candidates that could not be evaluated). The components lambda, lambda_path, cpdag and vstructures are NA or NULL here.

Details

The search is defined on the undirected layer: every candidate is a GGM support, and the edge scores that rank the candidates are those of the precision. A fit carrying the directed layer is refused rather than converted, since the conversion would silently replace the structure the caller fitted by a different one.

Candidates whose refit fails to converge or yields a non-finite criterion are skipped and recorded in the component candidate_failures.

See also

mc_select_lambda for the L1 route, mc_graph_stability for selection frequencies, mcg_selection-methods.

Other structure selection: mc_edge_scores(), mc_graph_penalized(), mc_graph_stability(), mc_select_lambda()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1); n <- 300
K <- diag(4) * 2; K[1,2]<-K[2,1]<- -0.6; K[2,3]<-K[3,2]<- -0.6; K[3,4]<-K[4,3]<- -0.6
Y <- matrix(rnorm(n * 4), n) %*% chol(solve(K)); x <- rnorm(n)
d <- data.frame(y1=Y[,1], y2=Y[,2], y3=Y[,3], y4=Y[,4], x=x)
f <- mcglm_graph(list(y1~x,y2~x,y3~x,y4~x), data = d)
#> Automatic initial values selected.
sel <- mc_graph_stepwise(f, criterion = "bic")
sel$n_edges
#> [1] 3
# }
